title: A dog bed for the cat
setting: Saturday morning at the door of Yuki's small rented flat. Satou-san, the elderly neighbour, turns up with a big parcel of hers that the driver took to his flat by mistake last night.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: yuki-san, ohayou gozaimasu. kinou no yoru, yuki-san no nimotsu ga uchi ni todoita n desu yo. heya o machigaeta mitai de.
lines.ja: ユキさん、おはようございます。昨日の夜、ユキさんの荷物がうちに届いたんですよ。部屋を間違えたみたいで。
lines.kana: ゆきさん、おはようございます。きのうのよる、ゆきさんのにもつがうちにとどいたんですよ。へやをまちがえたみたいで。
lines.english: Good morning, Yuki-san. Your parcel came to my place last night. They must have got the wrong flat.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: a, yokatta! kinou zutto matteta noni, nimotsu ga todokanakute. arigatou gozaimasu.
lines.ja: あ、よかった！昨日ずっと待ってたのに、荷物が届かなくて。ありがとうございます。
lines.kana: あ、よかった！きのうずっとまってたのに、にもつがとどかなくて。ありがとうございます。
lines.english: Oh, thank goodness! I waited in all day yesterday, and it never came. Thank you so much.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: kekkou ookii desu ne. nanika katta n desu ka?
lines.ja: けっこう大きいですね。何か買ったんですか？
lines.kana: けっこうおおきいですね。なにかかったんですか？
lines.english: It's quite big, isn't it? Did you buy something?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jitsu wa, inu no beddo na n desu. raishuu kara, inu o kau n desu.
lines.ja: 実は、犬のベッドなんです。来週から、犬を飼うんです。
lines.kana: じつは、いぬのべっどなんです。らいしゅうから、いぬをかうんです。
lines.english: It's a dog bed, actually. I'm getting a dog next week.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: hee, inu desu ka. demo, koko de inu o katte mo ii n desu ka?
lines.ja: へえ、犬ですか。でも、ここで犬を飼ってもいいんですか？
lines.kana: へえ、いぬですか。でも、ここでいぬをかってもいいんですか？
lines.english: Oh, a dog! But are you allowed to keep a dog here?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: hai. kono heya o kariru toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita.
lines.ja: はい。この部屋を借りるときに、小さい犬ならいいって言われました。
lines.kana: はい。このへやをかりるときに、ちいさいいぬならいいっていわれました。
lines.english: Yes. When I rented this place, they told me a small dog would be fine.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore wa yokatta desu ne. watashi mo mukashi, semai heya o karite, inu o katte imashita yo.
lines.ja: それはよかったですね。私も昔、狭い部屋を借りて、犬を飼っていましたよ。
lines.kana: それはよかったですね。わたしもむかし、せまいへやをかりて、いぬをかっていましたよ。
lines.english: That's good. Years ago I rented a poky little room too, and kept a dog in it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: uchi mo semai heya na node, chiisai inu ni shita n desu. beddo mo, netto de chanto shirabete kara kaimashita.
lines.ja: うちも狭い部屋なので、小さい犬にしたんです。ベッドも、ネットでちゃんと調べてから買いました。
lines.kana: うちもせまいへやなので、ちいさいいぬにしたんです。べっども、ねっとでちゃんとしらべてからかいました。
lines.english: My place is tiny too, so I went for a small dog. And I looked the bed up properly online before I bought it.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sasuga desu ne. donna beddo ka, mite mitai desu ne.
lines.ja: さすがですね。どんなベッドか、見てみたいですね。
lines.kana: さすがですね。どんなべっどか、みてみたいですね。
lines.english: How thorough of you. I'd love to see what it's like.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: jaa, ima dashite mimasu ne. semai heya desu kedo, douzo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、今出してみますね。狭い部屋ですけど、どうぞ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、いまだしてみますね。せまいへやですけど、どうぞ。
lines.english: Then I'll take it out now. It's a tiny place, but come on in.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: are? yuki-san, sono beddo, sugoku ookii desu ne.
lines.ja: あれ？ユキさん、そのベッド、すごく大きいですね。
lines.kana: あれ？ゆきさん、そのべっど、すごくおおきいですね。
lines.english: Oh? Yuki-san, that bed's awfully big.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e? uso! kore, ookii inu no beddo desu. machigaete tanonjatta mitai desu.
lines.ja: え？うそ！これ、大きい犬のベッドです。間違えて頼んじゃったみたいです。
lines.kana: え？うそ！これ、おおきいいぬのべっどです。まちがえてたのんじゃったみたいです。
lines.english: What? No way! This is a bed for a big dog. I must have ordered the wrong one.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: jaa, ookii inu o kattara dou desu ka?
lines.ja: じゃあ、大きい犬を飼ったらどうですか？
lines.kana: じゃあ、おおきいいぬをかったらどうですか？
lines.english: Well then, why not get a big dog?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kono semai heya de desu ka? muri desu yo. ookii inu nara, motto hiroi heya o karinai to.
lines.ja: この狭い部屋でですか？無理ですよ。大きい犬なら、もっと広い部屋を借りないと。
lines.kana: このせまいへやでですか？むりですよ。おおきいいぬなら、もっとひろいへやをかりないと。
lines.english: In this cramped little place? No way. A big dog would mean renting somewhere roomier.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore nara, sono beddo, uchi no neko ni moratte mo ii desu ka? tama wa, ookii beddo ga daisuki na n desu.
lines.ja: それなら、そのベッド、うちの猫にもらってもいいですか？タマは、大きいベッドが大好きなんです。
lines.kana: それなら、そのべっど、うちのねこにもらってもいいですか？たまは、おおきいべっどがだいすきなんです。
lines.english: In that case, could I have that bed for my cat? Tama loves a big bed.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: tama-chan ni desu ka? mochiron desu. jaa, chiisai beddo wa, inu ga kite kara, yousu o mite kaimasu ne.
lines.ja: タマちゃんにですか？もちろんです。じゃあ、小さいベッドは、犬が来てから、様子を見て買いますね。
lines.kana: たまちゃんにですか？もちろんです。じゃあ、ちいさいべっどは、いぬがきてから、ようすをみてかいますね。
lines.english: For Tama? Of course. Then I'll buy a small bed once the dog's here and I've seen how it settles in.

lines.speaker: satou
lines.romaji: sore ga ii desu ne. tsugi no nimotsu ga mata uchi ni todoitara, motte kimasu yo.
lines.ja: それがいいですね。次の荷物がまたうちに届いたら、持ってきますよ。
lines.kana: それがいいですね。つぎのにもつがまたうちにとどいたら、もってきますよ。
lines.english: Good idea. And if your next parcel turns up at my place again, I'll bring it round.

choices.english: The dog bed Yuki ordered for the small dog she's getting turns out to be for a big dog, so it goes to Satou-san's cat, and she'll buy a small one once the dog has come.
Yuki finds out dogs aren't allowed in her rented flat, so Satou-san offers to keep the dog at his place.
Satou-san ordered a big dog bed by mistake, so he gives it to Yuki for the small dog she's getting next week.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-4: Satou-san brings round Yuki's parcel, which went to his flat by mistake. It's a dog bed, because she's getting a dog next week (raishuu kara, inu o kau n desu). Lines 11-12: when she takes it out, it's a bed for a big dog, and she realises she ordered the wrong one (machigaete tanonjatta). Line 14: a big dog won't work in her cramped flat. Lines 15-16: Satou-san asks for the bed for his cat, Tama, and Yuki will buy a small one after the dog comes and she's seen how it settles in (yousu o mite). B is wrong: when Yuki rented the flat she was told a small dog would be fine (line 6), and Satou-san never offers to keep the dog. C swaps them round: it's Yuki's parcel (yuki-san no nimotsu, line 1), and the bed goes from Yuki to Satou-san's cat, not the other way.

questions.english: Satou-san asks if Yuki's allowed to keep a dog where she lives. What does she say?
questions.ja: ユキさんは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: When I let this flat out, they told me a small dog would be fine.
choices.romaji: kono heya o kasu toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita.

choices.english: When I hired this flat, they told me a small dog would be fine.
choices.romaji: kono heya o rentaru suru toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita.

choices.english: When I rented this flat, they told me a small dog would be fine.
choices.romaji: kono heya o kariru toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita.

questions.explanation: Line 6: kono heya o kariru toki ni, chiisai inu nara ii tte iwaremashita. Japanese has no separate verb for renting a place: the tenant kariru (borrows), the same verb as borrowing a pen. Satou-san uses it for the poky room he had years ago (semai heya o karite, line 7), and Yuki says a big dog would mean renting somewhere roomier (motto hiroi heya o karinai to, line 14). A is wrong: kasu (lend) is the landlord's side, so heya o kasu toki would mean when she let the flat out to someone else. B is wrong: rentaru suru is for hiring things like a car or a kimono for a day, not a flat you live in.

questions.english: You've just moved into a new flat, and Kenta has come round for the first time. At the door he says, "hee, koko ga atarashii heya? haitte ii?" (Oh, so this is the new place? Can I come in?) Invite him in the modest way a host does, saying it's a small place.
questions.ja: へえ、ここが新しい部屋？入っていい？
questions.kana: へえ、ここがあたらしいへや？はいっていい？
questions.romaji: hee, koko ga atarashii heya? haitte ii?
questions.answer: Use the host's set line with semai heya: semai heya da kedo, douzo (it's a tiny place, but come in).

modelAnswers.romaji: un, semai heya da kedo, douzo.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、狭い部屋だけど、どうぞ。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. It's a tiny place, but come on in.

modelAnswers.romaji: semai heya desu kedo, douzo haitte kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: 狭い部屋ですけど、どうぞ入ってください。
modelAnswers.english: It's only a small place, but please, come in.

questions.explanation: Yuki says just this to Satou-san in line 10: semai heya desu kedo, douzo. It's the host's modest welcome, and a guest will often answer hiroi ne! (it's roomy!). A cramped room or flat is semai, the opposite of hiroi, as in line 14 (kono semai heya de desu ka? ... motto hiroi heya). Chiisai heya is fine for a room's size (chiisai heya ga futatsu aru), but for the cramped feeling, and in this welcome, people say semai. Kenta's a friend, so da kedo. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Tanaka-san. Semai tokoro da kedo, douzo is a common variant.

questions.english: Kenta shows you photos of a friend's new puppy and says, "kawaii desho? inu, suki?" (Cute, right? Do you like dogs?) You love dogs, and your family has one at home. Tell him.
questions.ja: かわいいでしょ？犬、好き？
questions.kana: かわいいでしょ？いぬ、すき？
questions.answer: Say you love them, then say your family keeps one with inu o kau in the -teru form: uchi mo inu katteru n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, daisuki! uchi mo inu katteru n da.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、大好き！うちも犬飼ってるんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I love them! We've got a dog at home too.

modelAnswers.romaji: hai, daisuki desu. uchi de mo inu o katte iru n desu.
modelAnswers.ja: はい、大好きです。うちでも犬を飼っているんです。
modelAnswers.english: Yes, I love them. We have a dog at home too.

questions.explanation: Keeping a pet is kau, which sounds just like kau 'buy'. Yuki uses it for the dog she's getting (raishuu kara, inu o kau n desu, line 4), and Satou-san for the dog he had years ago (inu o katte imashita, line 7). His nanika katta n desu ka? in line 3 is the other kau, 'buy', and the context keeps them apart. Having a pet is almost always in the -teru form: inu katteru. Inu o motte iru sounds like you own a dog the way you own a bag, and inu ga iru (there's a dog) also works. The second model is the polite version, for someone like Satou-san.

questions.english: Satou-san brings Yuki her parcel. What had happened to it?
questions.ja: ユキさんの荷物は、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんのにもつは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san no nimotsu wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki was out when it came last night, so the driver left it with Satou-san next door.
The driver took it to Satou-san's flat by mistake last night, so it never reached Yuki, though she'd waited in all day.
It was left outside Yuki's door last night, and Satou-san took it in so it wouldn't go missing.

questions.explanation: Line 1: kinou no yoru, yuki-san no nimotsu ga uchi ni todoita n desu yo. heya o machigaeta mitai de. Todoku means 'reach', and here the parcel reached the wrong flat. Line 2: Yuki waited in all day, but nimotsu ga todokanakute (it never reached her). Things sent to you todoku, the same verb as for letters and messages. Tsuku is for people and trains getting somewhere (eki ni tsuku), so nimotsu ga tsuita is less usual. A is wrong: Yuki was in, waiting all day (zutto matteta), and the driver got the flat wrong. C is wrong: it never got to Yuki's door. It was delivered straight to Satou-san's place (uchi ni todoita).

newWords.english: bed (inu no beddo = a dog bed)
cat (uchi no neko = my cat; Satou-san's is called Tama)
